title: Diogenes the Cynic lived in a big clay jar, not a barrel: barrels didn’t exist yet

cover.alt: A modern statue in Sinop, Turkey, of Diogenes standing on a barrel, holding up a lamp, with a dog at his side.

body: Diogenes of Sinope, born around 400 BC on the Black Sea coast, made a philosophy of owning almost nothing. In Athens he slept in a pithos, a large ceramic jar normally used to store food. Later Latin writers, starting with Seneca, turned the jar into a ‘barrel’, and the picture stuck, even though wooden barrels did not exist in Greece in his day. His home town’s 2006 statue puts him on a barrel anyway, lamp in hand: he was said to walk the marketplace in daylight with a lit lamp, ‘looking for a man’, by which he meant a wise one.

slides.alt: A large Minoan clay storage jar, a pithos from Knossos, on display at the National Archaeological Museum of Athens.
slides.caption: A pithos from the storerooms of Knossos. Jars like this held food; Diogenes slept in one in Athens.

slides.heading: Stories told about him
items: Walked the market by day with a lamp, ‘looking for a man’
Told Alexander the Great to stand out of his sunlight
Plucked a chicken to mock Plato’s ‘featherless biped’

slides.heading: How much is true?
slides.text: Nearly everything we know comes from anecdotes collected centuries later, above all by Diogenes Laërtius in the 3rd century AD, and they vary in reliability. Even the tale that he was exiled from Sinope for ‘debasing the currency’ with his money-changer father may be partly fiction.

slides.question: What did Diogenes reportedly say when Alexander the Great offered him anything he wanted?
slides.explanation: ‘Yes, that you should stand a little out of my sun.’ Plutarch adds that Alexander replied that if he were not Alexander, he would be Diogenes.

slides.clue: The Greek word for the large storage jar that Diogenes lived in
slides.detail: A pithos held food. Wooden barrels came later, so the ‘barrel’ is a substitution by Latin writers, starting with Seneca.
